comments.typecheck: `vue-tsc`, not `tsc --noEmit` — for the same reason `examination` runs `ngc`: tsc compiles the TypeScript and never looks at a template, so a misspelled `mm-*` prop would go unchecked. vue-tsc checks SFC templates against the `GlobalComponents` declarations in src/types/design-system.d.ts.
comments.no-design-system-vue: There is deliberately no `@micro-medic/design-system-vue`. Vue 3 sets non-primitive values as DOM properties on unknown elements and binds `@mm-input` with addEventListener, so the `mm-*` elements need no binding layer — only the one-line `isCustomElement` predicate in webpack.config.js. That absence is the point: design-system-react exists because React has no prop for a custom event, and design-system-angular exists so strictTemplates can check bindings without CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA. Neither defect applies here.
comments.vue-tsc-peer: Watch vue-tsc's `typescript` peer range on install, the same trap as typescript-eslint: this repo is on TS 6, and a vue-tsc release whose peer range predates it will refuse to resolve.
